prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” lawyer for every truck-accident case — the right lawyer depends on your case facts and what you value (trial experience, record of big verdicts, resources for investigation, communication style, fees). I can help you find the best match. To start, please tell me:

- Where and when did the crash occur (city/county and date)?
- Were there serious injuries or fatalities?
- Was the truck a commercial vehicle (company name or markings) or a private truck?
- Any police report, photos, dashcam, or witness names available?
- Do you want a firm that’s local to Dallas or are you open to larger Texas firms that handle major truck cases?
- Any preferences (trial lawyer vs. settlement-focused, contingency fee only, language needs, budget)?

Meanwhile, quick guidance so you can evaluate lawyers right away:

What to look for
- Truck-specific experience: experience with FMCSA rules, cargo and logbook investigations, and claims vs. trucking companies and insurers.
- Trial experience and a history of sizable verdicts/settlements in commercial-vehicle cases.
- Resources: access to accident reconstructionists, medical experts, investigators.
- Fee structure: most serious firms take truck cases on contingency (no upfront fee; lawyer is paid a percentage of recovery).
- Track record and reputation: check peer reviews (Martindale-Hubbell), Super Lawyers, client reviews, and any disciplinary history (State Bar of Texas).
- Communication: clear case plan and regular updates.

Questions to ask at the first consult
- Have you handled truck accident cases like mine? What were results?
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?
- What investigators or experts will you use?
- What do you estimate my case is worth (range)?
- How do you charge and what costs am I responsible for?
- What’s the timeline and possible next steps?

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific recovery amount.
- No trial experience when you need a law firm willing to litigate.
- Poor communication or refusal to put fee agreement terms in writing.

Practical steps now
1. Preserve evidence: photos, medical records, police report, and any electronic data.
2. Note deadlines: in Texas, most personal injury claims must be filed within 2 years of the crash (shorter for government defendants).
3. Get 2–3 consultations. Most firms offer free initial meetings.

If you want, I can:
- Search and produce a short list (3–6) of well-rated Dallas personal injury/trucking lawyers or firms with contact info and quick notes about their experience, or
- Draft a set of tailored questions to take to consultations.

Which would you prefer?
